subject: biotechnology
chapter_title: An Overview of Recombinant DNA Technology

concepts.title: Recombinant DNA Technology Foundations
concepts.definition: Genetic engineering collects every method that edits nucleic acid directly, and it became practical once Stanley Cohen's plasmid delivery into E. coli met Herbert Boyer's restriction-enzyme cutting that leaves matching single-stranded termini - together, in 1973, they closed a foreign gene into a cut plasmid and created the first recombinant molecule, aided by ligase discovered in 1967.
concepts.key_idea: Cut with restriction enzymes, join with ligase, and carry the construct in a plasmid - the cut-paste-clone logic behind all rDNA work.
question_patterns: discuss briefly how recombinant DNA technology was initially developed
what expertise did Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer each contribute to the 1973 experiment
which enzymes act as molecular scissors on DNA and who discovered them
which enzyme joins two DNA fragments and in which year was it discovered
why did purified animal-sourced therapeutic proteins cause immunogenic reactions in humans
define gene cloning as the central theme of rDNA technology

solution_steps.explain: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites; ligase seals fragments together.
Cohen's plasmid transformation plus Boyer's sticky-end cutting produced the first recombinant plasmid.
Isolate a desired gene, propagate it in a host and harvest its product in quantity - gene cloning.

worked_examples.q: Who delivered plasmids into E. coli in the first recombinant experiment: Stanley Cohen or Herbert Boyer?

concepts.title: Milestones Timeline of Modern Biotechnology
concepts.definition: The subject advanced in dated leaps: Ereky coined the name in 1917, Avery's team fixed DNA as genetic material in 1944, Lederberg found plasmids in 1952, Watson and Crick solved the helix in 1953, Berg assembled the first recombinant DNA in 1972, Mullis invented PCR in 1983, Humulin won approval in 1982, the human genome project ran from 1990 to 2003, and the CRISPR-Cas9 Nobel arrived in 2019-2020 after the mRNA vaccine work.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract one milestone year from another to measure how fast the field moved between landmarks.
question_patterns: how many years did the Human Genome Project run from its 1990 start to its 2003 completion
how many years passed between the invention of PCR in 1983 and the CRISPR-Cas9 Nobel award year

arrange Berg's recombinant DNA Cohen-Boyer cloning and hybridoma technology in date order
in which year did Bt cotton reach India and who developed Golden Rice

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the launch year from the completion year.
Subtract the earlier technology's year from the later one.

concepts.title: Therapeutic Proteins from rDNA Technology
concepts.definition: Recombinant production replaced gland harvesting: where tons of pancreas once yielded only milligrams of insulin and thousands of pituitaries a little growth hormone, bacteria now brew human insulin (approved as Humulin in 1982) and growth hormone free of animal contaminants; interferon fights cancer while plasminogen activator and urokinase dissolve dangerous blood clots.
concepts.key_idea: Human genes in microbial hosts give safer, cheaper and limitless supplies of proteins once rationed from animal glands.
question_patterns: why was animal-sourced insulin limited in quantity and costly before recombinant production

how does interferon produced by rDNA technology serve cancer patients
what advantages do plant-made therapeutic proteins promise over animal-based ones

solution_steps.explain: Match the disease to its protein - diabetes to insulin, dwarfism to growth hormone, clots to activators.
Bacterial fermentation replaces animal glands, cutting cost and immunogenic contamination.
Humulin's 1982 FDA approval marks the first recombinant therapeutic.

worked_examples.q: Recombinant human insulin was approved under which name: Humulin or Flavr Savr?

concepts.title: E. coli Division versus Genome Replication Timing
concepts.definition: Escherichia coli finishes a division every twenty minutes yet needs about sixty minutes to copy its chromosome, an apparent paradox the cell resolves by running several replication forks in parallel (multifork replication), so each daughter still inherits a complete copy on schedule.
concepts.key_idea: Divide replication time by generation time to see how many forks must run at once.
question_patterns: E. coli divides in 20 minutes but takes 60 minutes to replicate its DNA - how many replication forks must run in parallel

how many generations of E. coli complete in two hours of growth
why is fast multifork replication vital for cloning plasmids in bacterial hosts
state the generation time of E. coli under standard conditions

solution_steps.explain: Forks needed equal replication minutes per generation minutes.
Elapsed minutes divided by the twenty-minute generation time.

concepts.title: Genetically Modified Crops and Plant Products
concepts.definition: Targeted edits in plant genomes gave farmers crops that shrug off disease, drought and salinity - the Flavr Savr tomato of 1994 opened the era, Monsanto's Bt cotton reached fields in 1996 and India by 2003, and Golden Rice carrying provitamin A appeared in 2000 - while rDNA technology now promises therapeutic proteins grown in plants at low cost and free of animal pathogens.
concepts.key_idea: One inserted gene can buy resistance, nutrition or shelf life - and plants may become the cheapest bioreactors of all.
question_patterns: name the first genetically engineered crop and the company that produced it
in which years was Bt cotton first released commercially and introduced into India
which crop was engineered to carry provitamin A and by whom
how does rDNA technology help farmers facing drought and salinity
list three disease-resistance or quality traits bred into GM crops
why are plant-based therapeutic products expected to be cheaper and safer than animal-based ones

solution_steps.explain: Resistance, tolerance, nutrition or shelf life identifies the crop example.
Flavr Savr 1994, Bt cotton 1996 (India 2003), Golden Rice 2000.
Higher quality produce, safer therapies and reduced pesticide or gland harvests.

worked_examples.q: Which tomato opened the GM crop era in 1994: Flavr Savr or Golden Rice?

solution_template.explain: Parallel forks equal replication time over generation time.
